findings.reason: The protected JavaScript solution recursively serializes valid JSON values into a compact string representation without using JSON.stringify. It pushes token chunks into an output buffer and joins them at the end. It properly distinguishes null, primitives, Array.isArray, and Object.keys iteration. The solution runs in O(S) time and O(S) space; no candidate is required.

Testing null before typeof value === 'object' prevents null from being misidentified as an object. Using Array.isArray ensures correct bracket formatting vs object brace formatting. Commas are conditionally inserted index > 0 to produce valid JSON syntax without trailing commas.

Appending tokens and performing a single final join takes O(S) time where S is output length. Output array buffer and call stack depth d <= 1000 use O(S) auxiliary space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts object JSON value, respects Object.keys property order, and returns a compact JSON string.

The approach accurately details type-driven JSON token generation, single-array buffer accumulation, 0-index comma placement, and O(S) time / O(S) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover recursive string concatenation overhead, manual stack frames, forbidden JSON.stringify, null handling precedence, Array.isArray distinction, empty containers, object key order, top-level primitives, and string escaping scope.
